candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication administration and client education
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — rivaroxaban administration
candidate.educational_objective: Teach the dose-specific food requirement for rivaroxaban 20 mg without incorrectly applying it to every rivaroxaban strength.

options.A: Take the 20 mg dose with food at approximately the same time each day because food improves absorption of this dose
options.B: Continue taking the 20 mg dose fasting because food substantially reduces rivaroxaban absorption
options.C: All rivaroxaban strengths must be taken fasting, so avoid meals for several hours after every dose
options.D: The relationship to food is unimportant for every rivaroxaban dose and indication

candidate.rationale: Current rivaroxaban labeling specifies that 15 mg and 20 mg tablets should be taken with food. For DVT/PE treatment, the 20 mg once-daily maintenance dose is taken with food at approximately the same time each day. Food increases exposure to the 20 mg dose; lower strengths such as 10 mg may be taken with or without food depending on the indication.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Rivaroxaban 20 mg requires administration with food for appropriate exposure; food requirements differ by dose.
candidate.source_locator: Sections 2.1 and 12.3: DVT/PE treatment 20 mg once daily with food; 15 mg and 20 mg tablets should be taken with food; food increases 20 mg bioavailability
candidate.stem: A client prescribed rivaroxaban 20 mg once daily for treatment of DVT says, ‘I usually take it before breakfast on an empty stomach.’ Which response by the nurse is best?
